findings.title: PHP Insecure Deserialization + IDOR - CTF Flag Extraction
findings.description: The application stores session data in a client-side cookie named 'data' as a base64-encoded PHP serialized UserProfile object. By decoding the cookie, modifying the userid field (e.g., from 4 to 1), re-encoding, and sending the forged cookie, an attacker can access any user's notes without authentication. This combines Insecure Deserialization with IDOR (Broken Object Level Authorization).

findings.title: IDOR - Full Data Exposure Across All User Accounts via Cookie Manipulation
findings.description: The PHP serialized cookie IDOR vulnerability allows enumeration of all user notes across all user IDs. No authentication beyond the initial session cookie is required to access any user's private notes. An attacker can iterate over user IDs 1-N to harvest all notes from all users.
findings.evidence:
UID=1 (admin): 2 notes including 'Flag' with content: FLAG{a68e6443c894f67f53c4db8f932273d21468c7acd52ee8e8a78357e88f3bccc5}
UID=2: 1 note
UID=3: 1 note (testuser)
UID=4: 1 note (hacker2 own account)
UID=5: 1 note
All notes accessed using forged data cookies with arbitrary userid values.
